chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who sleeps through fajr until the sun rises while he is traveling: what should he do? Is it permissible for him to make it up during the day? He said: “He does not make up, during the day, either a supererogatory prayer or an obligatory prayer. It is not permissible for him, nor is it valid for him. Rather, he delays it and then makes it up at night.”
So this is an anomalous report; the reports previously presented are not opposed by it, especially as they accord with the outward meaning of the Qur'an.

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: fajr, the dawn prayer time mentioned in the question
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report not relied upon against stronger narrations
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel, the state of being on a journey affecting the legal scenario
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ الْقُرْآنِ: the outward meaning of the Qur'an
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to make up a missed prayer

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about a traveler who misses fajr and makes it up after sunrise?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on a traveler who misses fajr by sleeping until sunrise and mentions a prohibition on making up that prayer during the day. The compiler then explicitly judges this report to be anomalous and not fit to oppose other reports he had already cited, which he says agree with the outward meaning of the Qur'an.
